mechanisms.label: Nuclear fuel sovereignty
mechanisms.summary: Recent public filings and agency announcements show a surge in U.S. domestic high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) enrichment activity, indicating that fuel availability is becoming a more immediate constraint for advanced reactor deployment.

observed_evidence.claim: The terminated NRC license SNM-7003 for the American Centrifuge Lead Cascade Facility authorized uranium enrichment up to 10 wt% U‑235 in up to 240 operating centrifuges.
observed_evidence.why_upstream: The license termination indicates that the facility’s enrichment capacity is no longer available, highlighting a potential shortfall in domestic enrichment capability.
observed_evidence.source_name: Centrus Energy Corp./American Centrifuge Operating, LLC (formerly USEC Inc.) Gas Centrifuge Enrichment Facility Licensing | Nuclear Regulatory Commission

observed_evidence.claim: Centrus Energy received a DOE award to support large‑scale production capacity for HALEU, with the first new capacity expected to come online by 2029.
observed_evidence.why_upstream: The award signals a deliberate expansion of domestic HALEU supply, directly addressing fuel availability for advanced reactors.
observed_evidence.source_name: ex991_haleu900mpr - SEC.gov

observed_evidence.claim: Under its NRC license, Centrus Energy may produce up to 600 kg of HALEU with enrichment up to 19.75 % U‑235, and Louisiana Energy Services may produce HALEU with enrichment up to 5.5 % U‑235.
observed_evidence.why_upstream: The licensed production limits quantify the current domestic HALEU output ceiling, underscoring the scale of fuel supply constraints.
observed_evidence.source_name: High-Assay Low-Enriched Uranium (HALEU) | Nuclear Regulatory Commission

observed_evidence.claim: The U.S. Department of Energy awarded contracts to six companies to build a domestic supply chain for HALEU fuels for advanced nuclear reactors.
